description.text: Too few lifeboats means a massive loss of life is imminent.

avoid.name: No Collision
description: The Titanic must not hit the iceberg.

debrief: At 23:40 on 14 April 1912, the Titanic passed the iceberg that should have sunk her. The collision is gone from the record.
In the crow’s nest and on the bridge, the Corps’ changes held.

debrief.text: The locker key never left the ship at Southampton.
A forgotten pair of glasses found its way from the purser’s drawer to the crow’s nest.
The locker in the crow’s nest was opened by a hand that history does not record.
With binoculars at hand, Frederick Fleet saw the berg while there was still time to act.
The Mesaba’s warning reached the bridge, and the officers were watching for ice dead ahead.

debrief: When Murdoch put the helm over, the engines kept driving ahead, and the ship answered in time.

More than 2,200 people will reach New York on Wednesday morning, and none of them will ever know how close they came. The Corps’ analysts, however, are uneasy. A history without the Titanic is a history without the lessons she taught.

debrief.text: The timeline shows no trace of the Corps’ interference.
Faint scars of paradox mark the places where agents crossed their own paths.

titanic_rescued.name: Titanic - Passengers Rescued
description: It is essential that the Titanic sinks, but the massive loss of life must be prevented.

collision.name: Collision
description: The Titanic must hit the iceberg.

debrief: At 02:20 on 15 April 1912 the Titanic went down, as history requires. This time, almost everyone she carried lived to see the morning.

Every davit on her boat deck carried a boat, and there was a seat for every soul aboard. The Californian heard the call for help and steamed through the ice toward the rockets, and her boats were among the first on the scene.
The disaster will still change the rules of the sea. In London, delegates from thirteen nations will write lifeboat rules for every ship, driven now by the story of a rescue rather than a massacre.

lusitania_nosink.name: Lusitania - Doesn't Sink
description: Prevent the sinking of the Lusitania.

afloat.name: Still Afloat
description: The Lusitania must not be sunk.

debrief: On the afternoon of 7 May 1915 the Lusitania rounded the Old Head of Kinsale and steamed on toward Liverpool.

debrief.text: Destroyers met her at the Fastnet, and no U-boat commander would risk a shot with warships at her side.
Running at full speed on a course no one could predict, she never gave U-20 a firing solution.
Kapitänleutnant Schwieger watched her pass out of range and turned for home with his last torpedoes unspent.

debrief: The 1,198 people who died off Kinsale will live. The sinking that hardened American opinion against Germany never happens, and what that means for the war is not yet clear.
